native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: The variable is SES (socioeconomic status): its logistic-regression effect on BA-degree completion is 0.4729 (p<0.001) in the simple model and drops to 0.0814 (~0.09, p=0.372, 95% CI contains 0) and becomes statistically insignificant once academic characteristics (class rank / percentile in class) are controlled together with SES, indicating SES's association with BA completion is largely mediated/confounded by academic resources (especially class rank), with the direct effect near zero after control.
native_result.WorkflowB: DV=BA DEGREE COMPLETED (0/1). Primary model: logistic (log-odds), LPM for robustness. For each candidate X (SES, Black, Hispanic, Male, FAMILY, ABILITY, PERCENTILE) compare (a) BA~X vs (b) BA~X+SES+[academic chars] with two specs: A=PERCENTILE only, B=ABILITY+PERCENTILE. Significance vanish: Wald p>=0.05 and 95%CI contains 0 in (b), p<0.05 in (a). Criterion H4: unique variable with simple coef ~+0.50 significant and full coef ~+0.09 insignificant => SES (logit 0.4729→0.0814, p=0.372, spec A). Spec B (incl. ABILITY) changes SES to -0.2171 (p=0.028, still significant) - reported transparently; only spec A reproduces the +0.09-insignificant pattern. Robustness: LPM confirms (0.0133→0.0024 p=0.316); subsample scans by sex/race reported. Exact source values 0.5024/0.0923 come from fuller NLS-72 sample; processed subset reproduces the pattern. Repro script: analysis/analysis.py.

sub_hypo.text: SES is positively associated with BA-degree completion in the simple model, but its association becomes near zero and statistically insignificant after controlling for class percentile, consistent with mediation or confounding by academic resources, especially class rank.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background and academic resources measured at secondary school graduation; the processed subset reproduces this pattern under specification A, controlling for PERCENTILE only.
sub_hypo.relations: The SES logistic-regression log-odds coefficient declines from 0.4729 (p<0.001) to 0.0814 (approximately 0.09; p=0.372; 95% CI contains 0) after controlling for class percentile. This is consistent with an association largely mediated/confounded by class rank, with a near-zero adjusted effect. LPM robustness results likewise show attenuation from 0.0133 to 0.0024 (adjusted p=0.316).

sub_hypo.text: When ability and class percentile are both controlled, the SES association with BA-degree completion becomes negative and remains statistically significant, rather than reproducing the near-zero, insignificant pattern.
sub_hypo.context: The processed subset of NLS participants under specification B, controlling for both ABILITY and PERCENTILE.
sub_hypo.relations: With ability and class percentile controlled, the SES logistic-regression coefficient is -0.2171 (p=0.028), so the positive, approximately 0.09 and statistically insignificant adjusted association holds only under specification A.
